newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedbank purchasing index rises in August.
newsitem.headline: Swedbank purchasing index rises in August.

text.p: Swedish investment bank Swedbank and logistics association Silf said on Monday their August purchasing managers' index was positive but did not yet show that the Swedish economy was recovering.
The August purchasing managers' index increased to 54.3 percent compared with 48.4 percent in July.
"The positive trend, particularly in export order intake and production, is anything but negligible," Swedbank and Silf said in a joint statement.
"The upturn in the index for these two key factors has actually gone on since February."

The index is a composite measure of factors such as order intake, production, planned production, employment and stocks, and is regarded as a good indicator of future development in the industrial economy.
The institutions pointed out that the period of upturn in the index is still too short to indicate a turnaround in the economy.
"We'd like to see a further upturn in the index in September and October to feel more secure on that point," Swedbank and Silf wrote.
